rv.q: There are times, though, when the play, directed by Vicky Featherstone, wavers and is in danger of coming to a standstill.
Her two daughters and teenage granddaughter have come round for fish and chips. Everyone sits gawping at their mobile telephones while they eat. The dialogue is skilful and the acting pretty good.
It's a distant rumble of thunder, a storm that never breaks.
Baffling. That's the only word to describe Michael Wynne's play...I kept waiting for something to happen. But hardly anything does.
Cuckoo catches the zeitgeist of the moment in a classically theatrical living room drama style.
Cuckoo is a play suffused with love, but also loneliness and existential dread...there’s an awful lot to love here, and the cast is sensational.
I predict they'd have more fun watching cat vids on their phones.
I recommend going to watch it if you're into dark humour and social commentary.
